Hello, my name is Mrs. Holborow, and welcome to Computing.
I'm so pleased you've decided to join me for the lesson today.
In today's lesson, we're going to be looking at the function of SQL and learning how to use SQL statements to insert and update data in a database.
Welcome to today's lesson from the unit Databases and SQL.
This lesson is called SQL fundamentals, and by the end of today's lesson, you'll be able to create SQL queries to insert and update data stored in a database.
Shall we make a start? We will be exploring these keywords throughout today's lesson.
SQL.
SQL, Structured Query Language, a decorative language designed for managing data held in a relational database management system.
INSERT.
INSERT, an SQL INSERT statement allows you to add data to pre-existing tables.
UPDATE.
UPDATE, an SQL UPDATE statement allows you to modify records.
Look out for these keywords throughout today's lesson.
Today's lesson is broken down into three parts.
We'll start by describing the function of SQL.
We'll then move on to insert new data using SQL statements and then we'll finish by updating data using an SQL statement.
Let's make a start by describing the function of SQL.
SQL stands for Structured Query Language.
It's a language used to communicate with a database.
You can use SQL to manipulate databases and retrieve records.
On the right-hand side of the screen, you can see some example SQL statements in the code block.
Aisha says, "Why do we need SQL?" Maybe pause the video here and have a think.
When you shop for items online, you'll typically be searching a database that uses SQL.
Your search terms will be added to SQL statements, and the relevant records will be retrieved from the database.
Can you think of any other examples of where you may have seen SQL statements? Common SQL operations include searching and retrieving records, inserting new records, deleting records, and updating records.
Time to check your understanding.
What does SQL stand for? Is it A, Structured Question Language, B, Sequential Query Logic, C, Structured Query Language, or D, System Query Line? Pause the video whilst you have a think of your answer.
Did you select C? Well done.
SQL stands for Structured Query Language.
SQL is widely used.
It's a standard language that comes in many varieties.
The most popular are MySQL and SQLite.
Fields in a database, as with variables in a programming language, have data types associated with them.
Data types specify the type of value the field can hold.
MySQL and SQLite provide different data types.
Let's have a look at them now.
Here are some MySQL data type examples.
So INT is an integer value.
FLOAT is a floating-point number, so a number with a decimal place.
VARCHAR is a string of variable length.
The x can be set by the user to set a maximum size.
DATE, a date value in the format year, year, year, year, hyphen, month, month, hyphen, day, day.
TIME, a time value in the format hour, hour, minute, minute, second, second.
Here are some examples of SQL data types.
INTEGER, an integer value.
REAL, a floating-point number, and TEXT, a string of variable length.
So note there are differences between the two.
Time to check your understanding.
Which SQL data type is used to store floating-point numbers? Is it A, INT, B, REAL, or C, FLOAT? Pause the video here whilst you have a think.
Did you select B? Well done.
REAL is used for floating-point numbers in SQLite.
FLOAT is used for floating-point numbers in MySQL.
It's important to note that there can be significant differences between some database implementations of SQL.
Okay, we are moving on to our first activity of today's lesson.
For part one, I'd like you to describe what SQL is and what it is used for.
For part two, a doctor's surgery stores data on patients.
Some of the fields from tblPatients, or table patients, are listed below.
Allocate an appropriate data type for each of the fields.
Note, if you use VARCHAR(x), you should suggest a maximum field size.
For example, VARCHAR(50) would allow a maximum of 50 characters to be entered.
So, the table below shows you the field titles.
We've got PatientID, Firstname, Surname, Date_of_birth, and Height in centimetres.
Provide the MySQL data type and the SQLite data type.
Pause the video here whilst you have a go at the tasks.
How did you get on with the tasks? Did you manage to describe what SQL is? Well done.
Let's have a look at a sample answer together.
SQL, which stands for Structured Query Language, is a programming language used to manage and interact with databases.
SQR is used to perform tasks such as retrieving data, for example, finding all users who scored more than 80 points in a game, adding new data like saving a new user's details when they sign up, updating, such as changing a password or username, and deleting data, like removing an account that is no longer needed.
Remember, if you need to pause your video here and make any amendments to your answer, you can do that now.
For the second part of task A, you were asked to look at the doctor's surgery data.
Some of the fields from the table patients were listed below and you were asked to allocate an appropriate data type for each of the fields.
So for PatientID, the MySQL data type would be INT and the SQLite data type would be INTEGER.
For Firstname, we've got MySQL data type as VARCHAR with a text limit of 20 characters.
And for SQLite, the data type of TEXT.
Similar for Surname, but this time we've given slightly more characters for the surname in MySQL.
And then in SQLite it's TEXT again.
Date_of_birth in MySQL, we can use the DATE data type.
But in SQLite, we don't have a DATE data type so we're going to use TEXT there.
And then lastly, for the Height in centimetres, in MySQL, we are going to use the FLOAT data type.
And in SQLite that is the REAL data type.
Remember the difference between the two there.
Okay, so we've described the function of SQL.
We're now going to move on to insert data using SQL statements.
An SQL INSERT statement allows you to add data into existing tables.
The basic syntax for an SQL INSERT statement is shown below.
So we have INSERT INTO table where would we would insert the name of the table, and then in brackets we have the field separated by commas.
On line two, we have the values that we're going to insert.
So again, these are stored inside brackets with a comma in between each one.
The statement allows you to specify one, the table where you want to insert data into, two, the fields to use, and three, which values to enter into those fields.
So let's have a look at this example.
So we have INSERT INTO tblFriends, or table friends, open brackets, firstname, surname, close brackets.
On line two, we have values, open brackets, and then we have Rachel, and then we have comma, and then we have Green, and then we're closing our brackets, and then we have a comma.
On line three, we have the next lot of data.
So again, inside brackets we have the values.
So we have Phoebe, comma, Buffay, closed brackets, another comma, so we're putting a comma in between each item, and then open our brackets again.
And then we have Chandler, comma, Bing, closed brackets.
Notice the semicolon at the end to indicate we finished that statement.
Also notice that because we're adding strings using this SQL statement, we're using the speech marks around the bits of text.
Time to check your understanding.
Which SQL command is used to add new data to the table? Is it A, UPDATE, B, ADD, C INSERT INTO, or D, SELECT? Pause the video whilst you have a think.
Did you select C? Well done.
INSERT INTO is the SQL command which is used to add new data into a table.
When you are inserting records, you must be careful to conform to any constraints that have been specified in the table design.
There may be fields that must not be left blank or that can only accept certain values.
A foreign key constraint may mean that another table will be checked for a matching primary key value.
You must also be aware of data types.
In this example, the activity_code and description are text fields.
So the values must be enclosed in quote marks, a bit like our names from the previous example.
assessment_fee is numeric, so must not be enclosed in quotes.
It is possible to add more than one record at a time by using a comma to separate each new set of values.
So you can see at the end of each line, on line three, four, and five, we have a comma before going down to the next line and inserting the new record.
True or false? It is not possible to add more than one record at a time using an SQL INSERT statement.
Pause the video here whilst you have a think.
Did you select false? Well done.
Why is that false? It is possible to add more than one record at a time, but remember you need to use a comma to separate each new set of values.
Okay, we're moving on to our second task of today's lesson.
You're doing a fantastic job so far, so well done.
The music download site has a database to hold customer download details.
The database is split into three tables, each with a primary key which is highlighted.
The tables have relationships, which are shown in the diagram.
So, on the left-hand side, we have the table called tblTracks.
In the middle we have the tblDownloads, and on the right-hand side we have the table called Members.
TrackID, which is the primary key in tblTracks, has a one-to-many relationship with the TrackID which is stored in tblDownloads.
MemberID, which is the primary key in tblMembers, has a one-to-many relationship with the MemberID in tblDownloads.
As the music downloads business grows, the database is in need of some administration.
Note, if you want to have a go at this practically, this database is provides as an additional resource for this lesson, but you will need to have access to a DBMS to perform the tasks.
Recent download data has just been passed to you.
So we have three records.
Consider which table you need to insert the data into.
Does all of the data provided above need to be entered? Write a script that will perform this action.
Pause the video whilst you complete the task.
How did you get on? Did you manage to write a script to insert the data? Well done.
So, you can see here we have an example script.
On line one, we have INSERT INTO tblDownloads.
Did you select the right table? And then in brackets, we have the fields that we need to insert data into.
So TrackID, MemberID, Date, and Time.
On line two, we have the first set of values that we're going to insert.
So we open our brackets, we have 11, and then comma, 53, comma, and then the date, and then comma, and then the time.
Close our brackets, and then we have another comma so that we can move on to the next record we want to insert.
So, first name, surname, and title are not contained in the tblDownloads, so we didn't need to insert that data into this table.
Remember, if you need to make any corrections to your statements, you can pause the video and do that now.
Okay, so we've described the function of SQL and we've inserted new data using SQL statements.
Let's now move on to update data using SQL statements.
An SQL UPDATE statement allows you to modify records.
The basic syntax for an SQL statement is shown below.
So, on line one we have UPDATE table where we'll specify the table we're updating.
On line two, we say SET field1, where the field is going to be replaced by the field name, is equal to, and then we have value1 and then we have comma, field2 = value2, field3 = value3, and so on.
Then, on line three, we have WHERE criteria.
Let's have a look at how this works in a bit more detail.
To update data in a table, you're required to specify the following.
One, the table which you intend to update, which is line one here.
Two, the new value that you want to set, and three, where a condition is being met.
So here's an example.
UPDATE tblEmployees.
SET password to equals, and then in our speech marks we've got the new password.
And then on line three, WHERE employeeid = 8.
So this is going to update employee eight's password.
Time to check your understanding.
What would be the outcome of running the following SQL statement on the data below? Look carefully at the SQL statement and the data and then have a go answering the question.
Did you spot it? Well done.
The SQL statement will change the mileage for both Ford Pumas.
So they will both end up having the mileage of 35,121.
That probably isn't what we wanted to do with the SQL statement.
How could you amend the SQL statement to only update the first Ford Puma in the table? The one that's highlighted.
Pause the video here whilst you have a think.

However, the vehicle registration is unique to each car, so that will only update the record you want it to.
So we've changed the SQL statement now, which says UPDATE vehicle, SET mileage, so those two lines are exactly the same, but our WHERE statement is different.
So WHERE vehicle_registration = 'DH19NBD'.
This will only update the first Ford Puma in the table.
Existing records can also be deleted from a table using an SQL DELETE statement.
The basic syntax for the DELETE statement is shown below.
So on line one, DELETE FROM table where we'll replace table with the table name, and then on line two, WHERE criteria.
Let's have a look at this in action.
To delete data from a table, you're required to specify the following.
One, the table which you intend to delete from, and two where a condition is being met.
So let's have a look at the example.
On line one, we have DELETE FROM tblStudents, and then on line two, we have WHERE date_of_birth, or date_of_birth, is less than 31/08/2002.
So this will delete any student whose date of birth is less than the 31st of August, 2002.
Okay, we're moving on to our last set of tasks for today's lesson, and you've done a fantastic job so far, so well done.

If you remove the records from tblDownloads, you are deleting the fact that the users downloaded the track in the first place.
This would cause problems if the user or company wanted to find out which tracks a member has downloaded.
It's important to be really careful and consider the actions if you are deleting data from a database.
Okay, we've come to the end of today's lesson, SQL fundamentals, and you've done a great job, so well done.
Let's summarise what we've learned together during today's lesson.
SQL stands for Structured Query Language.
It is a language used to communicate with a database.
You can use SQL to manipulate databases and retrieve records.
An SQL INSERT statement allows you to add data into pre-existing tables.
An SQL update statement allows you to modify records.
Existing records can be deleted from a table by using an SQL DELETE statement.
I hope you've enjoyed today's lesson, and I hope you join me again soon.
Bye.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Data is fundamental to any computer system.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: A primary key is an attribute that uniquely identifies a record in a database table, whereas a foreign key is an attribute in one table that is the primary key in another table and is used to link the tables together.

Hello, my name is Mrs. Holborow and welcome to Computing.
I'm so pleased that you've decided to join me for the lesson today.
In today's lesson, we are going to be investigating some key database terms, and we'll be comparing flat file and relational databases.
Welcome to today's lesson from the unit databases and SQL.
This lesson is called Database Fundamentals.
And by the end of today's lesson, you'll be able to describe the difference between a flat file and a relational database.
Shall we make a start.
We will be exploring these keywords throughout today's lesson.
Should we take a look at them? Record.
Record, a data structure that stores related fields of data for a single object or thing.
Field.
Field, the part of a record that is the category heading for data in a table, sometimes called an attribute.
Primary key.
Primary key, an attribute that uniquely identifies a record in a database table.
Foreign key.
Foreign key, an attribute in one table that is the primary key in another table, and that is used to link the tables together.
Look out for these key words throughout today's lesson.
Today's lesson is broken down into two parts.
We'll start by defining key database terms and then we'll move on to compare flat file and relational databases.
Let's make a start by defining key database terms. Data is fundamental to any computer system.
With data comes the need for a system that is able to store, sort, and search through it.
When large amounts of data need to be collected and organised, they are often stored in a database.
A database is a structured set of data.
It is structured in tables that are easy to search and update.
Here is an example of a flat file database.
This database holds the information about some song ID tracks.
A flat file database is a database that contains a single table.
So you can see here the data is stored in a table with the category headings, TrackID, title, artist and genre.
A table holds a collection of records for a particular theme.
In this case, it is a collection of music tracks.
The naming convention for a table always begins with a lowercase tbl, which stands for table, followed by the name of the table.
So in this example we have tblTracks.
A table contains a collection of records.
Each record contains the data for one object, person, or place.
In this example, each record is a single song track.
So you can see here the first record has the TrackID one, the title is "Float Away," the artist is The Springs, and the genre is pop.
That's one record.
The second record is TrackID two.
The title "In Denial," the artist Rocketts, and the Genre Rock.

A table has a number of fields.
These are the categories for each piece of data in the table.
This table has four fields, TrackID, title, artist, and genre.
Each record in the table needs a unique identifier, something that is a different piece of data from everything else.
A primary key is used to give each record a unique code.
In this example, the TrackID is the primary key, and you can see that the number is unique for each record.
Those numbers are not repeated.
A primary key can never be repeated.
This ensures that each record in the table is unique.
This is very important when dealing with thousands or even millions of records.

A flat file database is a database that has a single table.
The most common model for a database is a relational model.
A relational database contains more than one table.
The data in the table is linked using what we call relationships.
Relational databases can be used to solve some of the issues that occur in flat file databases.
Relationships can be one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many.
A one-to-one relationship means that one record in a table relates to a single record in another table.
A one-to-many relationship means that one record in a table relates to multiple records in another table.
A many-to-many relationship means that multiple records in a table relate to multiple records in another table.

A relational database lets you split data into smaller tables that link together.
This means no repeated data and it's easier to update.

With data comes the need for a system that is able to store, sort, and search through it.
A database is an organised collection of data.
Databases can be as simple as a single file and as complex as a set of related tables, each with multiple records, fields, and keys.

Bye.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: SQL is used to manage data within relational databases.
SQL allows users to interact with and interrogate data through standardised commands.
The SQL CREATE command can be used to create a new table.
SQL statements must follow specific syntax rules to execute correctly.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: SQL statements can be used to perform other actions on a databse such as creating new tables.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: SQL statements can only be used with exisiting tables.

00:12:03.180 --> 00:12:05.940
Common SQL operations include:

216
00:12:05.940 --> 00:12:08.220
searching and retrieving records,

217
00:12:08.220 --> 00:12:10.200
inserting new records,

218
00:12:10.200 --> 00:12:11.970
deleting records,

219
00:12:11.970 --> 00:12:13.803
and updating records.

220
00:12:15.450 --> 00:12:17.400
An SQL INSERT statement

221
00:12:17.400 --> 00:12:21.390
allows you to add data into pre-existing tables.

222
00:12:21.390 --> 00:12:26.190
The basic syntax for an SQL INSERT statement is:

223
00:12:26.190 --> 00:12:28.920
INSERT INTO table,

224
00:12:28.920 --> 00:12:31.860
followed by the field names in brackets,

225
00:12:31.860 --> 00:12:33.363
separated by commas.

226
00:12:34.350 --> 00:12:37.020
And then on line two: VALUES,

227
00:12:37.020 --> 00:12:39.750
with the values, again, stored in brackets

228
00:12:39.750 --> 00:12:41.613
and separated by commas.

229
00:12:44.580 --> 00:12:48.900
An SQL UPDATE statement allows you to modify records.

230
00:12:48.900 --> 00:12:53.370
The basic syntax for an SQL UPDATE statement is:

231
00:12:53.370 --> 00:12:54.630
UPDATE table,

232
00:12:54.630 --> 00:12:56.910
where table is the table name.

233
00:12:56.910 --> 00:12:57.990
Line two:

234
00:12:57.990 --> 00:13:02.990
SET field1 = value1, field2 = value2,

235
00:13:05.190 --> 00:13:07.140
and so on.

236
00:13:07.140 --> 00:13:10.620
And then on line three: WHERE criteria.

237
00:13:10.620 --> 00:13:14.613
So, what criteria are you looking for to do the update?

238
00:13:17.490 --> 00:13:21.300
You can use multiple criteria in your WHERE clause

239
00:13:21.300 --> 00:13:24.660
by using AND and OR operators.

240
00:13:24.660 --> 00:13:28.140
The AND operator or the OR operator

241
00:13:28.140 --> 00:13:30.690
specify the additional condition

242
00:13:30.690 --> 00:13:34.530
without specifying the WHERE keyword again.

243
00:13:34.530 --> 00:13:37.200
So let's have a look at that on line three:

244
00:13:37.200 --> 00:13:42.200
WHERE criteria OR criteria AND criteria.

245
00:13:42.630 --> 00:13:45.843
Notice we don't repeat the WHERE keyword.

246
00:13:48.270 --> 00:13:50.430
Note: In SQL statements,

247
00:13:50.430 --> 00:13:52.680
the AND operator takes precedence

248
00:13:52.680 --> 00:13:55.920
over the SQL Server OR operator,

249
00:13:55.920 --> 00:13:58.920
just like a multiplication operation

250
00:13:58.920 --> 00:14:02.820
takes precedence over an addition operation.

251
00:14:02.820 --> 00:14:05.550
Existing records can be deleted from a table

252
00:14:05.550 --> 00:14:08.460
using the SQL DELETE statement.

253
00:14:08.460 --> 00:14:12.420
The basic syntax for the SQL DELETE statement is:

254
00:14:12.420 --> 00:14:14.670
DELETE FROM table

255
00:14:14.670 --> 00:14:16.473
WHERE criteria.

256
00:14:17.610 --> 00:14:19.350
An SQL SELECT statement

257
00:14:19.350 --> 00:14:22.230
allows you to retrieve data from a database.

258
00:14:22.230 --> 00:14:26.100
The basic syntax for an SQL SELECT statement is:

259
00:14:26.100 --> 00:14:31.020
SELECT field1, field2, so on,

260
00:14:31.020 --> 00:14:35.010
where field1 and field2 are replaced by the field names.

261
00:14:35.010 --> 00:14:37.380
And then on line two: FROM table.

262
00:14:37.380 --> 00:14:39.480
So you are specifying the table

263
00:14:39.480 --> 00:14:42.183
that you are going to select the fields from.

264
00:14:43.650 --> 00:14:46.650
Rather than specifying the fields you want to be returned

265
00:14:46.650 --> 00:14:48.930
in specific search results,

266
00:14:48.930 --> 00:14:52.140
it is possible to select all available fields

267
00:14:52.140 --> 00:14:55.683
by using SELECT * or SELECT asterisk.

383
00:21:21.480 --> 00:21:23.977

385

386
00:21:29.130 --> 00:21:31.110
Let's summarise what we've learned together

387
00:21:31.110 --> 00:21:32.283
in today's lesson.

388
00:21:33.120 --> 00:21:37.642
SQL is used to manage data with relational databases.

389
00:21:37.642 --> 00:21:41.670
SQL allows users to interact with and interrogate data

390
00:21:41.670 --> 00:21:43.443
through standardised commands.

391
00:21:44.490 --> 00:21:49.023

392
00:21:50.010 --> 00:21:54.120
SQL statements must follow specific syntax rules

393
00:21:54.120 --> 00:21:56.430
to execute correctly.

394
00:21:56.430 --> 00:22:00.720
Missing commas, quotes, or incorrect keywords

395
00:22:00.720 --> 00:22:02.880
can cause errors.

396
00:22:02.880 --> 00:22:04.680
I hope you've enjoyed today's lesson

397
00:22:04.680 --> 00:22:07.353
and I hope you join me again soon. Bye.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Databases are designed to store large volumes of data.
This data could hold sensitive and personal information about individuals and needs to be protected.
In the UK there are a number of laws which protect data, including GDPR and The Data Protection Act.
Software can be categorised as open source or proprietary.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Proprietary software is usually sold to end users, although sometimes it is available for free.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Proprietary software always costs money.

lessons.transcript_sentences:
Hello, my name is Mrs. Holborow, and welcome to Computing.
I'm so pleased that you've been able to join me for the lesson today.
In today's lesson, we're going to be looking at some key UK laws on data and copyright, and we'll be explaining the difference between open source and proprietary software.
Welcome to today's lesson from the unit Databases and SQL.
This lesson is called Data protection, copyright, and the law.
And by the end of today's lesson, you'll be able to describe key UK computer laws and explain how they protect data, creative work, and software use.
Shall we make a start? We will be exploring these keywords throughout today's lesson.
Let's take a look at them now.
Patent.
Patent, a legal right that gives an inventor the exclusive right to make, use, or sell their invention for a certain number of years.
Open source.
Open source, software for which the programme source code is made available to the general public.
Proprietary.
Proprietary, software that is owned by a company or person.
You are not allowed to change, copy, or share it without permission.
Sometimes called closed source software.
Look out for these keywords throughout today's lesson.
Today's lesson is broken down into two sections.
We'll start by explaining key UK laws on data and copyright, and then we'll move on to compare open source and proprietary software.
Let's make a start by explaining key UK laws on data and copyright.
Databases are designed to store large volumes of data.
This data could include sensitive and personal information about individuals.
Aisha says, "I think it's important to protect this data.
What would happen if the database was hacked?" I think Aisha's right.
Here are four key documents that protect data and content.
The General Data Protection Regulation of 2018, the Data Protection Act of 2018, the Copyright Designs and Patents Act of 1988, and Creative Commons.
We will look at how these laws protect our data.
The General Data Protection Regulation, which is sometimes referred to as GDPR, in EU law, creates a European standard to protect individuals and regulates how companies and organisations may collect, hold, and use personal data.
The Data Protection Act 2018 is the UK's implementation of GDPR.
The Data Protection Act governs how the data of UK citizens can be collected, stored, and shared.
Those who collect data must follow the data protection principles.
Let's have a look at what these principles are.
The data protection principles ensures that data is used fairly and lawfully, for a specific and necessary purpose, and in a way that is adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: SQL stands for Structured Query Language. It is a language used to communicate with a database.
You can use SQL to manipulate databases and retrieve records.
An SQL SELECT statement allows you to retrieve data from a database.
The SQL SELECT * statement allows you to return all the data and fields from a table.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: You should only use the SELECT * query when all fields are needed. Including unnecessary data can be frustrating for the person viewing and working with the results.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Using SELECT * is always the best method for returning data from a database table.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can use SQL to retrieve data from a relational database.

teacherTips.teacherTip: This lesson can be completed without using a DBMS, but pupils could complete the activities practically using MySQL. Modelling concepts using software helps pupils appreciate why they are learning particular concepts.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A DBMS is a software application that allows a database administrator to maintain one or more relational databases.
A data model helps visualise how data is structured for a given scenario, including the relationships between elements.
One of the easiest ways to show how data is organised is by using an entity-relationship diagram (ERD).

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: While storage is a major function, a DBMS also provides data security, integrity and querying capabilities.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: A DBMS is only used for storing data.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can design a relational database structure for a given scenario.

lessonKeywords.description: performs calculations in a spreadsheet
tells you the location of a cell and is made from the column letter and row number, separated by a colon
a tool used in a spreadsheet to replicate cell data across a range of cells

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Formulas are used in spreadsheets to perform arithmetic calculations.
Cell references are used in formulas to use values stored in other parts of the spreadsheet.
Formulas that use cell references recalculate when the values in those reference cells change.
The fill handle tool can easily replicate formulas and data across a range of cells.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Using cell references within a formula means that the formula will recalculate when the values in those reference cells change.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Pupils may believe that each time data is changed in a spreadsheet the formulas will also need to be changed.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can use formulas in a spreadsheet to complete calculations.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Cell references used in formulas are like variables in programs and identify a location where a value is stored. Use the anaology of a labelled container to hold single value with pupils so that they can understand the importance of clear referencing.

lessonKeywords.description: a predefined formula that performs a calculation
a graphical representation of data

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A spreadsheet function is a predefined formula that performs calculations.
Spreadsheet functions can be used to analyse data.
Charts can be used to visualise data in a way that is easier to understand.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: If you want to reference the whole column you can remove the row numbers (e.g. A:A). Note that this is the only case where cell references do not have to follow the column:row convention.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: All range references in a spreadsheet needs to be the same as cell references in the format of column letter followed by row number (e.g. A1:A4).

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can analyse data using functions and summarise findings using charts.

teacherTips.teacherTip: All Oak resources can be customised to suit the local context of your school. Change the examples in the spreadsheet used for tasks to suit the interests of your class and to reflect the context of your local area.

lessonKeywords.description: a rectangular box that holds data in a spreadsheet
a vertical group of cells that runs from the top to the bottom
a horizontal line of cells that runs from left to right
modifying the appearance of data in a spreadsheet

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A spreadsheet is a tool used to store and analyse data.
In a spreadsheet, data is stored in cells, which are arranged in rows and columns.
Formatting can be applied to data in a spreadsheet to make the data easier to read and understand.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Spreadsheet cell references are presented as the combination of the column letter followed by the row number, (eg. A1, B2). If the order is interchanged any other part of the spreadsheet that references them will not be able to locate them.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: The order of column and row in a cell reference are unimportant as columns are labelled with letters and rows are labelled as numbers.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can identify the components of a spreadsheet and apply formatting to improve the presentation of data.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Pupils could extend the flag creation exercise by providing instructions to a partner and then testing out each others instructions to create the flag.

lessonKeywords.description: applies a style or format to a cell based on whether a cell matches a certain criteria

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Conditional formatting applies a style or format to a cell based on whether a cell matches a certain criteria.
Conditional formatting can be applied to specific data in a range of cells.
Conditional formatting can be used to highlight or pick out key pieces of data.
Spreadsheet tools can be combined to analyse and present data.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Conditional formatting can be used to apply a range of formatting a cell including the text of the cell itself.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Pupils may think that conditional formatting can only be used to add background colour to a cell.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can use conditional formatting and a range of tools to present data effectively.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Conditional formatting is often seen in the world around us to draw attention to when changes require humans to take notice for example, the crossing at a set of traffic lights. Encourage pupils to identify examples they have seen themselves to appreciate the usefulness of this formatting technique.

lessonKeywords.description: arranging data into a meaningful order
given criteria used to show a subset of a data set
a predefined formula that performs a calculation

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Data can be sorted in ascending or descending order.
Filters can be applied to hide data that is not needed for a purpose.
A sort or filter can be applied to a data set to make it easier to analyse or visualise information.
A function is a predefined formula in a spreadsheet that can help with calculations.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: A filter can be applied to data to remove selected data from a data set. However, this data is not permanently removed, if the filter is taken off the data will still be there.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: When a filter is applied to a data set the data that is filtered is removed permanently.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can use spreadsheet tools to sort and search data to find and analyse information.

teacherTips.teacherTip: The file available for this lesson is based on data from a previous Olympic Games. The data set can be easily changed if you feel pupils in your school would relate better to a different example.

lessonKeywords.description: facts and figures in their raw form
data that has been given structure or meaning
collecting data yourself
someone else collects the data

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Data is just the raw values and facts, presented without any meaning.
Information is data that has been given structure or meaning.
Data you collect yourself is primary data.
Data collected by others is secondary data.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Data and information are realted but are different. Data is raw facts and figures whilst information is data that has been processed to have meaning.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Data and information are the same thing.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can explain the difference between data and information and know that data can come from a range of sources.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Data collection can be a time consuming process. AI tools are good at generating data and you could create data sets for pupils upon request. If using a spreadsheet, pupils could then copy and paste the data.

lessonKeywords.description: a combination of two or more logic gates used to represent a more complex logical statement
a table showing the outputs for all possible combinations of inputs to a logic gate or logic circuit

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Boolean logic is the foundation of all digital circuit design.
A logic circuit is a set of two or more logic gates that are connected to implement more complex logic.
A digital electronic circuit in a computer system is typically made up of millions of logic gates.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Logic gates can be combined to created complex circuits that represent any number of logic statements combined.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: As logic gates are limited to two input, logic statements should also be limited in the same way.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can combine logic gates to build circuits.

teacherTips.teacherTip: If learners find it difficult to draw logic circuits, you could use an online tool as an alternative allowing them to test their circuits as they build them.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A logic circuit is a set of two or more logic gates that are connected to implement more complex logic.
A digital electronic circuit in a computer system is used to realise solutions to problems.
A circuit diagram illustrates how logic gates are combined to create digital circuits.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Remind pupils of how the order of precedence in maths is applied to calculations. In a similarway, logic gates should be evaluated in the order: brackets, NOT, AND, OR.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Pupils often find it difficult to know what order logic gates should be evaluated. Without brackets, there is still an order of precedence.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can create circuit diagrams to represent logic circuits that solve a problem.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Pupils could underline inputs, outputs and logic in a statement and then order them before constructing the circuit diagram. Tasks will always have some elements of these as clues as to what to build expressions for.

lessonKeywords.description: a table showing the outputs for all possible combinations of inputs to a logic gate or logic circuit
an expression that evaluates to either True or False

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A truth table is a way of summarising and checking the logic of a circuit.
The table shows all possible combinations of inputs and, for each combination, the output the circuit will produce.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: A truth table can have column headings that calculate the value of the expression, for example (A OR B).
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: A truth table can only have the column headings of single inputs like A, B, or X.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can construct a truth table to represent a Boolean expression or circuit.

teacherTips.teacherTip: The process of constructing a truth table is modelled in the lesson. Encourage pupils to start by identifying the column headings and then all the possible combinations of input.

lessonKeywords.description: a piece of software that allows you to build a logic circuit and test it with different input values
a picture used to represent a more complex logical statement

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Logic gate simulator software allows you to create an interactive circuit diagram.
You can test that the circuit you have created is correct by changing the inputs and observing the output.
A logic gate simulator can help you quickly generate a truth table for a logic circuit.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Logic gates can be combined to create complex circuits that represent any number of logic statements combined. This can involve the same input being connected to multiple logic gates.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Each input can only be wired to one logic gate.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can use logic gate simulator software to model logic circuits.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Model how to create and test the use of an online logic gate simulator for example logic statements. Show how the inputs of a truth table are controlled in the software and how the output of the curcuit can be determined.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: A logic statement is a statement that evaluates to either True or False.
You can write a logic statement to represent an outcome where the result is dependent on Boolean variables.
Boolean logic combines multiple logic statements into an expression that is either True or False.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Boolean operators have an order of precedence that affects the which operator applies to which variable. If a different order is required, brackets should be used.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Boolean logic statements should be processed in the order they are read (from left to right).

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can evaluate and develop logic statements using Boolean logic.

teacherTips.teacherTip: A visualiser is useful to model how descriptive statements can be reduced down to a set of variables and Boolean operators. Pupils benefit from understanding how this abstraction process is carried out.

lessonKeywords.description: an expression that evaluates to either True or False
an electronic component that carries out a logical operation
a table showing the outputs for all possible combinations of inputs to a logic gate or logic circuit

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Boolean logic is a form of algebra where all logical relations can be expressed as a combination of AND, OR and NOT.
A logic gate is a fundamental component of a digital circuit.
Each logic gate has a symbol, which is used in circuit diagrams.
Each logic gate has a unique truth table that shows how the output changes with different inputs.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: The number of inputs depends on the logic gate. The NOT gate is different in that it only has one input.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: All logic gates have two inputs and one output.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can identify different logic gates and construct the truth table for each logic gate.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Get students into the practice of writing out the possible inputs for a truth table as if they were counting in binary. For the AND and OR gates this is 00, 01, 10, 11.

lessonKeywords.description: a combination of two or more logic gates used to represent a more complex Boolean expression
a table showing the outputs for all possible combinations of inputs to a logic gate or logic circuit

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Boolean logic is the foundation of all digital circuit design.
A logic circuit is a set of two or more logic gates that are connected to implement more complex logic.
A digital electronic circuit in a computer system is typically made up of millions of logic gates.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Logic gates can be combined to created complex circuits that represent any number of logic statements combined.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: As logic gates are limited to two input, logic statements should also be limited in the same way.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can combine logic gates to build circuits.

teacherTips.teacherTip: If learners find it difficult to draw logic circuits, you could use an online tool as an alternative allowing them to test their circuits as they build them.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: The three fundamental Boolean operators are AND, OR and NOT. These are used in programs to perform selection and control program flow. In Python, these are written in words as: and, or, not.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Boolean logic is only used in logic circuits and logic gates.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Boolean statements are based on human language and can be articulated to understand when they are true. lessons.lessonTitle: The cost of cyber crime and hacker motivation

lessonKeywords.description: any illegal activity that involves a computer, network, or digital device
someone who uses their computer skills to access systems or networks, sometimes to fix problems, and sometimes to cause harm
a group of people who live together in a community and follow shared rules, values, and systems
something that is done on purpose to harm, damage, or hurt someone or something

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Cybercrime causes financial loss to individuals, businesses, and governments.
Cyber attacks can stop essential services and impact public safety.
Hackers are motivated by a range of factors.
Cybercrime affects society as a whole, creating fear, reducing trust in digital systems and impacting mental well-being.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Not all hackers are malicious. There are different types of hackers such as white hat ethical hackers, grey hat hackers who may break rules but not for personal gain and black hat hackers who are malicious hackers who exploit systems illegally.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: All hackers are criminals trying to steal or destroy data.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe hacker motivations and the costs of cybercrime

teacherTips.teacherTip: Use a short, engaging news video or real world examples of cybercrime (e.g. the WannaCry ransomware attack) to show the financial and emotional impact of cybercrime. Then, guide students in identifying who the victims were, what was lost, and what might have motivated the attacker.

In general, hackers fall within one of the following categories: white hat ethical hackers, grey hat hackers, or black hat malicious hackers.
A white hat hacker is an ethical hacker who uses their computer skills to protect systems and data.
They work to find and fix security problems before malicious hackers can take advantage of them and cause harm.
White hat hackers have permission to do their work and are often employed by companies and governments.
They are motivated by helping others to improve their security.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Encryption is the process of converting data into an unreadable format to prevent unauthorised access.
There are many different algorithms that can be used to encrypt data.
Encryption protects personal data and keeps messages private, ensuring security during online transactions.
Encryption is used in messaging services, HTTPS websites and banking apps.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Encryption greatly improves security, but it is not foolproof. If encryption keys are weak, stolen or mismanaged, encrypted data can still be accessed by attackers.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Encryption makes data completely safe and unbreakable.

Let's make a start by describing encryption.
Encryption is the process of encoding data or a message, so that it cannot be understood by anyone other than the intended recipient.
Encryption is used as a security measure to protect information from being read or tampered with by others.
To encrypt data or information, an encryption algorithm is used.
An encryption algorithm is a set of rules that transforms readable data called plaintext into unreadable data called ciphertext.
Plaintext is the original, readable version of a message or data before it has been encrypted.
The meaning of the text or data can be easily understood by anyone who sees it, which is why it needs encryption to keep it private.
Ciphertext is the scrambled, unreadable version of a message or data that has been encrypted using an algorithm.

Without the key, it's extremely difficult to decrypt scrambled data.

lessonKeywords.description: malicious software - a program designed to cause damage to computer systems, corrupt or change files, steal data or cause disruption to services
to spread something harmful like a virus or malware into a system
the act of taking something that doesn’t belong to you, without permission and with no intention of giving it back
the money cybercriminals demand after locking files or systems

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Malware is malicious software designed to harm, steal, or disrupt computer systems.
There are different types of malware, including viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware, and adware.
Each type of malware works differently, but they often trick users into downloading or installing them.
Malware can cause serious damage, such as data loss, system failure or financial loss.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Malware can infect any idevice that is connected to the internet, including smartphones, tablets and smart TVs. Mobile malware is increasingly common and can steal data, track location or lock users out of their devices — just like on computers.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Malware only affects computers, not phones or tablets.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe malware and explain how it attacks systems.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Incorporate storytelling to explain how malware spreads and impacts victims. Turn famous or recent malware incidents into short, engaging stories. Storytelling helps students remember key concepts and see the human side of cybersecurity threats, making lessons more impactful.

Malware is any program or file that is created to damage, steal from, or take control of a computer system without the user's permission.

They often trick users into downloading or installing them, in order to infect the system.
Viruses are a malicious form of self-replicating software.
Once a computer or network is infected, the virus will replicate itself by maliciously modifying other computer programs and inserting code.
Worms replicate themselves but do not attach themselves to files like a virus does.
Instead, worms spread through the network and use the system's resources.
Most worms cause problems by using up network bandwidth and therefore slowing down the network significantly.
A trojan is a piece of software that appears to perform a useful function, such as a game or an update.
Trojan malware is named after the Trojan Horse story, as it disguises itself as something harmless to trick users into allowing it into their system, just as the wooden horse was used to secretly infiltrate Troy.
Ransomware is a form of virus that takes advantage of a security vulnerability in an operating system, application, or any other software code.

00:02:19.140 --> 00:02:23.340
Andeep says, "Wait, I'm not sure that's a good idea.

43
00:02:23.340 --> 00:02:25.680
Maybe we should hand it to a teacher

44
00:02:25.680 --> 00:02:27.147
so it can be checked."

45
00:02:28.050 --> 00:02:31.080
Aisha says, "I'm not sure what to do.

46
00:02:31.080 --> 00:02:32.813
I want to know what's on the USB stick

47
00:02:32.813 --> 00:02:34.740
and who it belongs to,

48
00:02:34.740 --> 00:02:37.887
but maybe it's safer to hand it in to a teacher."

49
00:02:39.780 --> 00:02:42.180
What option would you choose?

50
00:02:42.180 --> 00:02:45.270
Option one: plug it into a computer

51
00:02:45.270 --> 00:02:48.660
or option two: hand it in to a teacher?

52
00:02:48.660 --> 00:02:50.520
Maybe pause the video whilst you have a think

53
00:02:50.520 --> 00:02:51.720
about what you would do.

54
00:02:57.750 --> 00:02:59.820
Let's explore what would happen.

55
00:02:59.820 --> 00:03:03.270
Option one, you plug it into a computer to try

56
00:03:03.270 --> 00:03:05.103
and find out who it belongs to.

57
00:03:06.030 --> 00:03:10.050
When you plug it in, the light starts flashing instantly,

58
00:03:10.050 --> 00:03:13.143
but no file explorer window appears.

59
00:03:15.690 --> 00:03:19.260
Then you see a red screen appear with a message saying

60
00:03:19.260 --> 00:03:22.353
that the data on the school network has been encrypted.

61
00:03:25.980 --> 00:03:27.870
As you look around the room,

62
00:03:27.870 --> 00:03:29.910
you see the same message appear

63
00:03:29.910 --> 00:03:32.163
on all the computers in the room.

64
00:03:33.990 --> 00:03:37.860
By plugging in the USB stick without getting it checked,

65
00:03:37.860 --> 00:03:40.233
a security breach has happened.

66
00:03:42.750 --> 00:03:46.830
Option two: you walk past a teacher on duty,

67
00:03:46.830 --> 00:03:51.273
explain the situation and hand over the USB stick to them.

68
00:03:52.830 --> 00:03:55.893
The teacher passes it to the IT support team.

69
00:03:58.200 --> 00:03:59.940
The network manager runs it

70
00:03:59.940 --> 00:04:02.010
through a special piece of software

71
00:04:02.010 --> 00:04:03.630
that scans it for malware.

72
00:04:03.630 --> 00:04:06.240
Before any executable files

73
00:04:06.240 --> 00:04:08.553
are allowed to be exposed to the network.

74
00:04:10.890 --> 00:04:14.280
They find that the USB drive contains malware

75
00:04:14.280 --> 00:04:17.493
that would have infected the entire school network.

76
00:04:19.470 --> 00:04:22.530
By handing in the USB stick to the teacher,

77
00:04:22.530 --> 00:04:25.173
a security breach has been prevented.

78
00:04:27.720 --> 00:04:31.170
Aisha says, "I'm really pleased I chose option two

79
00:04:31.170 --> 00:04:34.050
and gave the USB stick to a teacher.

80
00:04:34.050 --> 00:04:35.220
The network manager found

81
00:04:35.220 --> 00:04:39.780
that the USB stick contained malware that would have caused

82
00:04:39.780 --> 00:04:42.267
all of the school's data to be encrypted."

83
00:04:43.770 --> 00:04:47.130
Sam says, "That was a good choice, Aisha.

84
00:04:47.130 --> 00:04:49.350
I didn't realize that the USB stick

85
00:04:49.350 --> 00:04:52.050
might harm the school network.

86
00:04:52.050 --> 00:04:54.987
Did you say malware? What's that?"

87
00:04:57.150 --> 00:05:01.500
Malware or malicious software is software that is designed

88
00:05:01.500 --> 00:05:06.090
to gain access to your computer with malicious intent.

89
00:05:06.090 --> 00:05:08.940
Malware can infect whole networks

90
00:05:08.940 --> 00:05:11.553
or a single digital device.

91
00:05:13.620 --> 00:05:16.360
Malicious intent includes things like

92
00:05:17.250 --> 00:05:21.540
disabling hardware, stealing data,

93
00:05:21.540 --> 00:05:26.540
forced advertising, sending email spam,

94
00:05:26.580 --> 00:05:28.143
or extorting money.

95
00:05:30.300 --> 00:05:32.460
Malware is any program

96
00:05:32.460 --> 00:05:36.270
or file that is created to damage, steal from,

97
00:05:36.270 --> 00:05:38.940
or take control of a computer system

98
00:05:38.940 --> 00:05:40.983
without the user's permission.

99
00:05:43.290 --> 00:05:46.080
Malware is created by cyber criminals

100
00:05:46.080 --> 00:05:49.890
for their own personal gain or to cause harm.

101
00:05:49.890 --> 00:05:54.510
However, not all malware is created by cyber criminals

102
00:05:54.510 --> 00:05:55.983
for the same reason.

103
00:05:58.560 --> 00:06:02.520
Black hat hackers may want to steal money, data,

104
00:06:02.520 --> 00:06:04.203
or personal information.

105
00:06:05.400 --> 00:06:09.153
Hacktivists may want to make a political statement.

106
00:06:10.170 --> 00:06:13.800
Cyberspies may intend to gain secret information

107
00:06:13.800 --> 00:06:15.663
for governments or companies.

108
00:06:17.520 --> 00:06:19.860
Time to check your understanding.

109
00:06:19.860 --> 00:06:24.860
Malware is A: a harmless file on a computer,

110
00:06:25.140 --> 00:06:29.160
B: software designed to harm or steal data,

111
00:06:29.160 --> 00:06:33.060
or C: software that is difficult to install?

112
00:06:33.060 --> 00:06:35.193
Pause the video whilst you have a think.

113
00:06:42.000 --> 00:06:43.320
Did you select B?

114
00:06:43.320 --> 00:06:44.610
Well done.

115
00:06:44.610 --> 00:06:48.243
Malware is software designed to harm or steal data.

116
00:06:50.040 --> 00:06:51.570
True or false?

117
00:06:51.570 --> 00:06:55.080
Malware can infect whole networks of devices

118
00:06:55.080 --> 00:06:57.990
or single digital devices.

119
00:06:57.990 --> 00:07:00.093
Pause the video whilst you have a think.

120
00:07:06.990 --> 00:07:09.360
Did you select true? That's right.

121
00:07:09.360 --> 00:07:10.193
Well done.

122
00:07:13.007 --> 00:07:14.437
Andeep says,

123
00:07:14.437 --> 00:07:18.900
"So USB devices can infect a system with malware,

124
00:07:18.900 --> 00:07:21.057
but what other ways can it happen?"

125
00:07:21.960 --> 00:07:26.460
Infected files can be downloaded from unsafe websites,

126
00:07:26.460 --> 00:07:30.873
email attachments, or fake apps by accident.

127
00:07:32.910 --> 00:07:36.090
Clicking a link on a fake or hacked website

128
00:07:36.090 --> 00:07:39.003
can download malware and infect a system.

129
00:07:39.960 --> 00:07:44.433
Pirated or fake software can often contain hidden malware.

130
00:07:45.750 --> 00:07:48.210
Using outdated software

131
00:07:48.210 --> 00:07:51.330
or failing to use antivirus protection

132
00:07:51.330 --> 00:07:54.693
increases the risk of malware infecting a system.

133
00:07:56.880 --> 00:08:00.930
Connecting to unsafe Wi-Fi networks can allow attackers

134
00:08:00.930 --> 00:08:04.083
to send malware through public networks.

135
00:08:06.240 --> 00:08:11.130
Once malware gets into a system, it can hide, spread

136
00:08:11.130 --> 00:08:13.113
and start doing damage.

137
00:08:13.950 --> 00:08:17.820
Malware can cause serious damage such as data loss,

138
00:08:17.820 --> 00:08:21.333
system failure or financial loss.

139
00:08:23.130 --> 00:08:24.900
True or false?

140
00:08:24.900 --> 00:08:29.130
Connecting to unsafe Wi-Fi networks can allow an attacker

141
00:08:29.130 --> 00:08:32.520
to send malware through public networks.

142
00:08:32.520 --> 00:08:34.520
Pause the video whilst you have a think.

143
00:08:41.460 --> 00:08:43.740
That's right. It's true.

144
00:08:43.740 --> 00:08:46.710
And often companies restrict individuals

145
00:08:46.710 --> 00:08:50.133
from connecting to unsafe Wi-Fi networks,

146
00:08:51.180 --> 00:08:53.850
and if you do connect to a Wi-Fi network,

147
00:08:53.850 --> 00:08:57.843
they may suggest you use a secure VPN to do so.

148
00:08:59.430 --> 00:09:03.420
Okay, we've come to the first task of today's lesson

149
00:09:03.420 --> 00:09:07.110
and I'd like you to explain, what is malware

150
00:09:07.110 --> 00:09:10.380
and how can it affect a computer network?

151
00:09:10.380 --> 00:09:12.180
Pause the video whilst you have a go

152
00:09:12.180 --> 00:09:13.533
at answering the question.

153
00:09:19.860 --> 00:09:23.130
How did you get on? Did you manage to answer the question?

154
00:09:23.130 --> 00:09:26.913
Well done. Let's have a look at a sample answer together.

155
00:09:27.780 --> 00:09:30.930
Malware is short for malicious software.

156
00:09:30.930 --> 00:09:33.060
Malware is any type of software

157
00:09:33.060 --> 00:09:36.540
that is designed to cause harm, steal information

158
00:09:36.540 --> 00:09:39.720
or disrupt a computer or network.

159
00:09:39.720 --> 00:09:43.320
Once a device or network is infected with malware,

160
00:09:43.320 --> 00:09:48.320
it could disable hardware, steal data, send email spam,

161
00:09:48.930 --> 00:09:53.190
or ask for a ransom to unlock files or systems.

162
00:09:53.190 --> 00:09:56.820
There are lots of ways malware can infect devices,

163
00:09:56.820 --> 00:10:01.170
such as through malicious downloads, email attachments,

164
00:10:01.170 --> 00:10:06.170
fake or hacked websites, or unsafe networks.

165
00:10:06.420 --> 00:10:08.850
Remember, if you need to pause your video

166
00:10:08.850 --> 00:10:12.543
and add extra detail to your answer, you can do that now.

167
00:10:18.810 --> 00:10:21.750
So, so far we've described malware.

168
00:10:21.750 --> 00:10:23.940
We are now going to move on to explain

169
00:10:23.940 --> 00:10:27.330
how malware attacks systems.

170
00:10:27.330 --> 00:10:29.970
There are many types of malware.

171
00:10:29.970 --> 00:10:31.440
Do you know of any?

172
00:10:31.440 --> 00:10:34.040
Maybe pause the video whilst you have a quick think.

173
00:10:40.320 --> 00:10:43.170
Did you think of any types of malware?

174
00:10:43.170 --> 00:10:45.870
Let's have a look at some together now.

175
00:10:45.870 --> 00:10:48.903
So, viruses, spyware, ransomware,

176
00:10:50.970 --> 00:10:55.230
trojans, adware, and worms.

177
00:10:55.230 --> 00:10:56.910
Did you have any of those?

178
00:10:56.910 --> 00:10:58.923
Are any of these terms familiar to you?

179
00:11:01.200 --> 00:11:03.450
Each type of malware works differently,

180
00:11:03.450 --> 00:11:05.583
depending on what they are designed to do.

181
00:11:08.610 --> 00:11:12.480
They often trick users into downloading or installing them,

182
00:11:12.480 --> 00:11:14.583
in order to infect the system.

183
00:11:16.020 --> 00:11:20.553
Viruses are a malicious form of self-replicating software.

184
00:11:23.670 --> 00:11:26.820
Once a computer or network is infected,

185
00:11:26.820 --> 00:11:29.310
the virus will replicate itself

186
00:11:29.310 --> 00:11:33.060
by maliciously modifying other computer programs

187
00:11:33.060 --> 00:11:34.743
and inserting code.

188
00:11:36.810 --> 00:11:39.180
Worms replicate themselves

189
00:11:39.180 --> 00:11:43.233
but do not attach themselves to files like a virus does.

190
00:11:44.370 --> 00:11:47.550
Instead, worms spread through the network

191
00:11:47.550 --> 00:11:49.893
and use the system's resources.

192
00:11:51.030 --> 00:11:55.620
Most worms cause problems by using up network bandwidth

193
00:11:55.620 --> 00:11:59.433
and therefore slowing down the network significantly.

194
00:12:01.470 --> 00:12:04.110
A trojan is a piece of software that appears

195
00:12:04.110 --> 00:12:08.973
to perform a useful function, such as a game or an update.

196
00:12:09.840 --> 00:12:14.370
Trojan malware is named after the Trojan Horse story,

197
00:12:14.370 --> 00:12:18.060
as it disguises itself as something harmless

198
00:12:18.060 --> 00:12:21.900
to trick users into allowing it into their system,

199
00:12:21.900 --> 00:12:24.180
just as the wooden horse was used

200
00:12:24.180 --> 00:12:26.613
to secretly infiltrate Troy.

201
00:12:29.280 --> 00:12:32.700
Ransomware is a form of virus that takes advantage

202
00:12:32.700 --> 00:12:36.840
of a security vulnerability in an operating system,

203
00:12:36.840 --> 00:12:40.053
application, or any other software code.

204
00:12:42.060 --> 00:12:46.200
Ransomware locks a computer, encrypts files

205
00:12:46.200 --> 00:12:50.040
and prevents the user from being able to access the data

206
00:12:50.040 --> 00:12:51.993
until a ransom is paid.

207
00:12:54.330 --> 00:12:56.700
Time to check your understanding.

208
00:12:56.700 --> 00:13:00.090
What do viruses and worms have in common?

209
00:13:00.090 --> 00:13:03.690
Is it A: they're both self-replicating,

210
00:13:03.690 --> 00:13:06.690
B: they both encrypt data,

211
00:13:06.690 --> 00:13:10.740
or C: they both display unwanted adverts?

212
00:13:10.740 --> 00:13:12.873
Pause the video whilst you have a think.

213
00:13:19.230 --> 00:13:22.050
Did you select A? Well done.

214
00:13:22.050 --> 00:13:25.473
Both worms and viruses are self-replicating.

215
00:13:27.630 --> 00:13:30.660
Spyware is unwanted software that monitors

216
00:13:30.660 --> 00:13:33.000
and gathers information on a person

217
00:13:33.000 --> 00:13:34.893
and how they use their computer.

218
00:13:35.820 --> 00:13:38.880
This can include monitoring your internet usage

219
00:13:38.880 --> 00:13:41.853
to send you harmless but annoying adverts.

220
00:13:42.690 --> 00:13:46.320
More sinister spyware will include keyloggers

221
00:13:46.320 --> 00:13:49.653
that record every keystroke made by a user.

222
00:13:51.690 --> 00:13:53.490
Adware refers to software

223
00:13:53.490 --> 00:13:57.003
that has advertisements embedded in the application.

224
00:13:58.590 --> 00:14:00.840
This is not always a bad thing

225
00:14:00.840 --> 00:14:04.110
and is considered a legitimate alternative

226
00:14:04.110 --> 00:14:06.360
that can be offered to consumers

227
00:14:06.360 --> 00:14:08.433
who do not wish to pay for software.

228
00:14:10.410 --> 00:14:13.800
Adware can become a problem when it goes beyond

229
00:14:13.800 --> 00:14:16.920
showing harmless ads and starts affecting

230
00:14:16.920 --> 00:14:18.813
your device or privacy.

231
00:14:20.880 --> 00:14:25.050
Adware becomes malware when it invades privacy,

232
00:14:25.050 --> 00:14:29.670
reduces performance, or is designed to install itself

233
00:14:29.670 --> 00:14:31.893
and be difficult to uninstall.

234
00:14:34.500 --> 00:14:36.780
Time to check your understanding.

235
00:14:36.780 --> 00:14:39.750
Which type of malware hides inside software

236
00:14:39.750 --> 00:14:41.850
that appears to be useful?

237
00:14:41.850 --> 00:14:46.850
Is it A: worm, B: trojan, or C: virus?

238
00:14:48.030 --> 00:14:50.163
Pause the video whilst you have a think.

239
00:14:56.820 --> 00:14:59.880
Did you select trojan? Well done.

240
00:14:59.880 --> 00:15:02.763
Remember the story of the Trojan Horse.

241
00:15:05.190 --> 00:15:07.620
Which type of malware encrypts files

242
00:15:07.620 --> 00:15:12.150
and prevents access to the data until the victim has paid?

243
00:15:12.150 --> 00:15:17.150
Is it A: worm, B: trojan, or C: ransomware?

244
00:15:17.370 --> 00:15:19.593
Pause the video whilst you have a think.

245
00:15:26.070 --> 00:15:29.473
That's right. The correct answer is C: ransomware.

246
00:15:30.750 --> 00:15:34.710
Okay, we are moving on to our final task of today's lesson.

247
00:15:34.710 --> 00:15:37.830
I'd like you to complete the table to describe the methods

248
00:15:37.830 --> 00:15:40.590
of attack for each type of malware.

249
00:15:40.590 --> 00:15:44.812
So we have virus, worm, spyware,

250
00:15:44.812 --> 00:15:47.493
ransomware, trojan, and adware.

251
00:15:48.330 --> 00:15:51.003
Pause the video whilst you complete the table.

252
00:15:58.500 --> 00:15:59.333
How did you get on?

253
00:15:59.333 --> 00:16:02.880
Did you manage to complete the table? Well done.

254
00:16:02.880 --> 00:16:05.613
Let's have a look at some sample answers together.

255
00:16:06.480 --> 00:16:10.920
So for virus, the method of attack is replicates itself

256
00:16:10.920 --> 00:16:14.253
by modifying other programs and inserting code.

257
00:16:15.150 --> 00:16:17.310
A worm spreads through the network

258
00:16:17.310 --> 00:16:20.430
and uses the system's resources.

259
00:16:20.430 --> 00:16:23.340
Spyware gathers information on a person

260
00:16:23.340 --> 00:16:25.263
and how they use their computer.

261
00:16:26.280 --> 00:16:30.090
Ransomware locks a computer, encrypts files

262
00:16:30.090 --> 00:16:34.290
and prevents access to data until a ransom is paid.

263
00:16:34.290 --> 00:16:38.310
Trojan disguises itself as something harmless

264
00:16:38.310 --> 00:16:42.930
to trick users into allowing it onto their system.

265
00:16:42.930 --> 00:16:47.040
Adware is installed with other applications.

266
00:16:47.040 --> 00:16:49.770
Remember, if you need to pause your video here

267
00:16:49.770 --> 00:16:53.643
and add any extra detail to your table, you can do that now.

268
00:16:59.640 --> 00:17:02.010
We've come to the end of today's lesson,

269
00:17:02.010 --> 00:17:04.170
Malware: malicious software,

270
00:17:04.170 --> 00:17:07.290
and you've done a fantastic job, so well done.

271
00:17:07.290 --> 00:17:09.540
Let's summarize what we've learned together

272
00:17:09.540 --> 00:17:11.670
during today's lesson.

273
00:17:11.670 --> 00:17:16.470
Malware is malicious software designed to infect, harm,

274
00:17:16.470 --> 00:17:20.190
steal or disrupt computer systems.

275
00:17:20.190 --> 00:17:24.510
Malware can cause serious damage such as data loss,

276
00:17:24.510 --> 00:17:27.993
system failure, or financial loss.

277
00:17:28.920 --> 00:17:32.670
There are different types of malware, including viruses,

278
00:17:32.670 --> 00:17:37.563
worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware, and adware.

279
00:17:38.790 --> 00:17:42.450
Each type of malware works differently,

280
00:17:42.450 --> 00:17:44.940
but they often trick users into

281
00:17:44.940 --> 00:17:47.910
downloading or installing them.

282
00:17:47.910 --> 00:17:49.770
I hope you've enjoyed today's lesson

283
00:17:49.770 --> 00:17:51.660
and I hope you join me again soon.

284
00:17:51.660 --> 00:17:52.493
Bye.

lessonKeywords.description: a deliberate attempt to damage, disrupt or gain unauthorised access to computer systems, networks or data
to check and clean user input to stop harmful code or to delete data to stop it being recovered or misused
the main software that manages a computer’s hardware and allows other programs to run
weaknesses in a system, software or network that can be exploited by attackers to gain unauthorised access, cause damage or steal data

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Software can be designed and updated to prevent cyberattacks.
Techniques like input sanitisation, modular testing and code reviews can be used to prevent cyberattacks.
Encryption protects data by making it unreadable without the correct key.
Strong passwords and two-factor authentication add important layers of security against unauthorised access.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Antivirus software is helpful, but it’s only one part of a broader defence strategy. Full protection also requires regular software updates, strong passwords, safe browsing habits and user awareness to avoid phishing and suspicious downloads.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Installing antivirus software is enough to fully protect my device from malware.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe how to defend against malware and suggest ways to improve security.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Give learners analogies with concepts and routines they will already understand in the real world. For example, installing antivirus software is like locking your front door, or updating software security is like getting a vaccine to protect you from viruses.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Social engineering is a cybercrime that manipulates people into revealing confidential information.
Social engineering targets human psychology rather than exploiting technical systems.
There are many different social engineering techniques such as blagging, phishing and pharming.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Social engineering mainly targets human psychology, not technical vulnerabilities. It's more about exploiting trust and human error than technical skills.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Social engineering only involves technical hacking or complex cyberattacks.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe social engineering and explain the techniques used in social engineering.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Use real life scenarios or role playing activities to help students understand how social engineering works. For example, simulate a phishing email or fake phone call and have students identify red flags and discuss what they would do.

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Ciphers are used to encrypt and decrypt messages, turning readable text into unreadable ciphertext.
Common ciphers like the Caesar and substitution ciphers use patterns or keys to shift or replace letters in a message.
More complex ciphers use multiple shifts or a keyword, making them harder to break.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Ciphers are one type of encryption method. Encryption includes ciphers but also involves algorithms, keys, and protocols used in modern digital security systems.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Ciphers and encryption are the same thing.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe how common ciphers work, and use them to encrypt and decrypt information.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Use fun, hands-on activities like decoding secret messages with the Caesar cipher or creating simple substitution ciphers. These activities help students understand how encryption works by letting them see and experience the process of turning plaintext into ciphertext and back.

lessons.lessonTitle: Testing as a form of defence

lessonKeywords.description: a simulated cyberattack used to test the security of a computer system, network or application
the measures and practices used to protect systems, networks and data from unauthorised access, damage or theft
a cybersecurity professional who is authorised to break into systems in order to find and fix vulnerabilities
the process of monitoring and analysing computer network traffic to gather information and detect intrusion

keyLearningPoints.keyLearningPoint: Penetration testing is a controlled method of testing a system’s security by simulating real cyberattacks.
Penetration testing helps identify and fix vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them.
There are different types of penetration tests, including black box, white box and grey box.
Penetration testing is a key part of maintaining strong cybersecurity in organisations.

misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.response: Penetration testing is legal and ethical when done with permission. It's a form of ethical hacking used to help organisations find and fix security weaknesses before real hackers exploit them.
misconceptionsAndCommonMistakes.misconception: Penetration testing is illegal or the same as hacking.

lessons.pupilLessonOutcome: I can describe and design a penetration test.

teacherTips.teacherTip: Use real-world analogies like testing a house for weak locks or open windows to explain how penetration testers look for vulnerabilities in a system. Then, guide students through a simple, controlled scenario such as identifying weaknesses in a mock website or app.
